name: Reduction firing
summary: A kiln fires with too little air, so that the flames take oxygen from the glaze and the clay. Iron turns green or black, and copper turns red.
how: Close the damper and the air inlets in the high part of the firing.
Let the flames fill the kiln with carbon monoxide.
Keep the reduction for 1 to 3 hours at about 1000 to 1300 °C.
Open the air and cool the kiln slowly.

origin.note: Potters at the Yue kilns fire green-glazed stoneware in a kiln with a smoky, low-air flame.

adoptions.via: Bernard Leach builds a Japanese climbing kiln at St Ives and fires ash and celadon glazes in reduction at 1280 °C.
